technical.title: Technical Supply
technical.desc: Which application and valve details help us assess a request. A technical enquiry guide.
technical.lead: A valve is chosen for an application, not from a product description alone. This guide shows which details help us assess your request. It does not replace engineering approval.
guide_rows: Ball, butterfly, gate or check. If unsure, describe what the valve must do.
Nominal diameter, for example DN50 or 2 inch.
Pieces required, and whether this is a one-off or repeat need.
What flows through the valve: water, oil, gas, chemical, solids.
Working and design pressure, and any pressure class required.
Body, seat and trim materials, or the medium so we can discuss options.
Flanged, threaded, wafer, lug or welded, with standard if known.
Applicable standards, datasheets, drawings, certificates required.
Destination and the date you need the valves.
technical.notes_p: We check your details for completeness, ask for what is missing, and confirm that a credible supply option exists. Documents are reviewed against the actual product before any offer.
technical.limits_p: It does not provide automatic technical recommendations or engineering approval. Suitability is confirmed against your actual application and requirements.

process.title: How Sourcing Works
process.desc: From requirement review to supply coordination. What happens after you send an enquiry.
process.lead: One enquiry process, with a person reviewing at each stage. This is what happens after you submit.
steps: Five required fields. Add technical details and files if you have them.
You receive a reference number once your enquiry is stored.
We check technical completeness and ask for anything missing.
We confirm whether a credible supply option exists for your requirement.
Specifications, terms and delivery assumptions are reviewed by a person before an offer is sent.
We follow up on the offer and coordinate the process toward delivery.
process.note: No quotation is sent without human review. Timing depends on the request and is not promised on this site.

why.title: Why Revalx
why.desc: What working with REVALX looks like. Benefits shown only once approved.
why.lead: Five working principles, shown for review. Each claim needs approval and evidence before launch.
points: Four valve categories instead of a catalogue of everything.

Sourcing and supply coordination run through a single enquiry.

rfq.title: Request a Quote
rfq.desc: Send a valve enquiry. Five required fields. Technical details are optional.
rfq.lead: Five fields are required. The technical details are optional, but each one helps us assess your request faster. You can submit with incomplete information.
rfq.why_p: Size, medium, pressure, temperature and materials let us check that a supply option can fit the application. If you do not know them yet, leave them blank and describe the need.
rfq.after_p: You receive a reference number. A person reviews your enquiry and contacts you. No quotation is sent without review.

contact.title: Contact and Privacy
contact.desc: Contact details and privacy information for REVALX.
contact.lead: The quickest way to reach us is the enquiry form. Direct contact details will be published once approved.
details_rows: Use the Request a Quote form
contact.privacy_p: The enquiry form collects your name, company, email, country and the details you provide, including any files you upload. We use them to respond to your enquiry. Retention periods, your rights and the data controller are to be confirmed by REVALX before launch.
privacy_list: Uploaded files are stored privately and are not publicly accessible.
The form does not require an account.
Cookie and analytics information will be added if analytics are used.
